source.title: Improving LLM Safety Alignment with Dual-Objective Optimization
source.authors: Xuandong Zhao; Will Cai; Tian-Neng Shi; David Huang; Li-Cong Lin; Song Mei; D. Song

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study directly evaluates prefilling and suffix jailbreak success and token-position KL patterns, but uses its own training methods and experimental setup rather than explicitly reproducing either original study.
record.gate_note: The paper reports attack-success rates for prefilling, multi-turn, GCG and AutoDAN attacks, and describes token-position KL patterns. It also describes fine-tuning a separate model on 110 harmful samples to generate harmful training responses, but reports no measured harmful-compliance outcome for that induced model; this is not evidence for V1. Alpaca is used as utility-retention data, not as a test of benign fine-tuning eroding safety. No weight-localization test is reported. The text includes prompts for an LLM judge, not instructions directed at an AI reading or reviewing this paper.
record.test_reason: The study measures prefilling and transferred-suffix attack success on safety-trained Llama-3-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-2B-It (V4). It trains models with harmful-prefix augmentation and compares token-position KL and ASR across objectives (V6, V7). It uses a different method from the originals, aimed at the same questions.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that DPO's loss is suboptimal for refusal learning. They find that DOOR/W-DOOR (prefix-augmented refusal SFT plus NPO unlearning, with token weights) markedly cut prefilling and suffix ASR with gains on multi-turn attacks. They also find robustness correlates with larger, deeper token-distribution shifts and with representation separation. They claim utility is maintained and see no clear over-refusal trade-off over extended training, while noting augmentation may cause some over-refusal.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces DOOR/W-DOOR training with harmful-prefix augmentation, NPO unlearning and token-level weights; evaluates against original and baseline alignment methods rather than reproducing the original fine-tuning or KL measurement protocols exactly.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by alignment method, model, and attack type. Prefilling ASR varies with prefill length (Figures 2 and 10); multi-turn robustness weakens as turn count increases. The paper reports that token-weight function/parameter variants in Figure 13 did not materially change robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: t-SNE of layer-16 Gemma activations: W-DOOR separates safe and harmful token representations more than DPO or the original model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Deeper safety alignment coincides with greater representational separation of harmful and safe content.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The KL-position results are shown graphically without extracted numeric values. No uncertainty estimates or significance tests are reported in the provided text. Multi-turn evaluation uses approximately 100 curated harmful interactions per model, and the authors say robustness gains there are marginal. The distribution-shift/robustness relationship is presented as a correlation, not a causal isolation.
record.rows_left_out: Did not transcribe the full per-prefill-length curves in Figures 2 and 10 or the variant curves in Figure 13 because exact numeric values are not stated; Table 1's attack results and the text's descriptions are recorded instead. Capability and over-rejection benchmark outcomes are omitted because they do not directly measure the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: A model copy fine-tuned on 110 HEx-PHI harmful samples is used only to generate data. Its compliance rate is not reported.
Alpaca appears only as retain data. No benign-only fine-tuning safety test.
No KL between aligned and pretrained base models. The KL reported is relative to the instruct model after extra safety tuning.
Decoding changes are not tested. Suffix attacks are only transferred from the base model.
Durability against further fine-tuning attacks is not tested. Only two small models.

missing.what: Average log-prob of safe tokens after a harmful prefix and of harmful tokens over 100 positions. DPO lowers safe-token probability below the original; W-DOOR forgets harmful tokens at later positions.
DPO gradient decomposition showing the effective learning rate for refusals saturates, versus a constant rate under DOOR.
Multi-turn ASR by number of turns: other methods rise with turns, W-DOOR does not.

record.verdict_notes: The record's single V4+V7 state per row was ambiguous: low ASR after training is 'absent' for V4 but 'observed' for V7. I relinked trained-model rows to V7 only, original/RR/TAR rows to V4, and multi-turn original rows to none. The K rows were wrongly linked to V3 and marked 'reversed'. Their KL is relative to the instruct model after extra safety tuning, so they bear on V6 (DPO/NPO shallow) and V7 (augmentation deepens). Table 1 DPO is the augmented variant. Multi-turn eval data were filtered on base-model success, and suffix attacks were transferred from the base model. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: No safety-trained model is tested for compliance after fine-tuning on a few to a few hundred harmful examples. The separate harmful-response model is induced to generate harmful responses for data construction, with no reported compliance-rate result.
No test measures harmful compliance after ordinary or carefully chosen benign-only fine-tuning. Alpaca data is used as a utility-retention component alongside safety alignment.
The paper reports qualitative KL-by-position patterns for its methods and training data, not a general result across aligned/base model families, prompts, or response-generation settings.
Prefilling and suffix attacks (GCG and AutoDAN) and multi-turn attacks are evaluated. Decoding changes are not evaluated.
No test localizes safety to a small set of weights, parameters, or ranks.
The paper analyzes DPO gradients and reports associations between training method, token distributions, and robustness; it does not isolate the proposed mechanisms in a causal experiment.

The paper tests DOOR/W-DOOR training and attack robustness, including suffix and multi-turn settings, and reports KL patterns. It does not directly establish that a particular token-depth change causes robustness or persists across other models and training regimes.
